text: The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, how is the wood of the vine better than any other wood, the branch that grows among the trees of the forest?
Is any of its wood taken to make something useful? Does anyone take from it a peg to hang a vessel on?

versions.text: Is any of its wood taken to make something useful? Does anyone make from it a peg to hang a vessel on?
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb in the second clause is the same verb 'take' (יִקְחוּ) as in the first clause, not 'make'. Keeping 'take' preserves the repetition and the sense that nothing at all is drawn from the vine wood.

text: See—it is given to the fire as fuel. The fire consumes both its ends, and its middle is charred. Is it good for anything then?

versions.text: No—it is thrown into the fire as fuel. The fire consumes both its ends, and its middle is charred. Is it good for anything then?
versions.explanation: 'No—' supplies an answer that the Hebrew does not state; the text opens with הִנֵּה ('behold/see'). Also the verb is 'given' (נִתַּן), not 'thrown'. 'See—it is given' keeps the rhetorical movement while staying closer to the wording.

text: When it was whole, nothing could be made of it; how much less, now that the fire has consumed it and it is charred!

versions.text: If it was useless when it was whole, how much less can anything be made of it once the fire has consumed it and it is charred!
versions.explanation: The Hebrew states a fact introduced by הִנֵּה ('behold'), not a condition ('if'). Rendering it as a statement is more accurate and also reads more crisply aloud.

text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire as fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will set my face against them. Though they have come out of the fire, the fire will yet consume them. And you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.
I will make the land a desolation, because they have been utterly unfaithful, declares the Lord GOD.
